CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left ankle pain following fall.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who sustained a left ankle injury yesterday while on a walk with his wife. He stepped off a curb and landed on his left ankle incorrectly. He denies hearing a pop but reports feeling the ankle extended and stretched. Pain is localized to the outside of the ankle. He was able to ambulate back to his house but with significant pain. Pain has been present for a couple of days and is described as severe, rated 8/10 without medication, improving only slightly to 7/10 with ibuprofen or acetaminophen. He has been treating the injury with ibuprofen, elevation, ice, and weight-bearing restriction. Denies prior significant ankle injuries.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports pain with weight-bearing and ambulation. Vitals noted to be slightly elevated, attributed to pain.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No prior substantial ankle injuries reported.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen (as needed for pain)
Acetaminophen (as needed for pain)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works from home. He and his wife are active, taking walks regularly. Recently increased activity since COVID-related remote work began.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: Stable with slight elevation. Left ankle exam reveals ecchymosis and swelling over the lateral malleolus with edema present. Tenderness to palpation on the lateral side with soft tissue swelling. No joint laxity appreciated. No bony tenderness on palpation of foot. Neurovascular exam: Capillary refill brisk (less than 3 seconds), strong dorsalis pedis pulses bilaterally, motor and sensation intact bilaterally and symmetric.

RESULTS
Left ankle X-ray: No fracture or bony abnormalities identified.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left ankle lateral ligament sprain. Continue RICE protocol (rest, ice, compression, elevation). Provide air cast for ankle stabilization. Prescribe crutches with instructions to remain off affected leg but begin walking as tolerated. Continue NSAIDs for pain and swelling management. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess progress. Patient instructed to return if pain worsens or does not improve as expected.
